solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Maybe crib letters and corner support?

parts.note: a crib is one example of a bed, a cot for a baby
letters delivered to you are post, the mail

explanation.surface: A baby's cot, some letters and a prop in a corner: a jumble from a nursery clear-out.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall post at each corner of a bed frame holds up the bed and any canopy.

clue.text: Here in Africa, unworldly character — old, religious — advanced to accept greeting

indicators.note: the earlier string takes the later piece inside it, as a host accepts a guest

parts.note: ET is the extra-terrestrial of the Spielberg film, a being not of this world
pi is informal for pious or religious
A is an abbreviation for advanced, as in A level
hi is a casual greeting

explanation.surface: An alien, old and devout, steps forward to receive a welcome somewhere in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: The greeting sits between the first two letters and the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition asks for a place on the African continent, and this country in the Horn of Africa is one.

clue.text: Col above left giving means of access

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits above the second in the grid

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
port is the left-hand side of a ship

explanation.surface: A mountain col high above the valley on the left offers a way through.
explanation.definitionFit: A travel document grants its holder entry into foreign countries, so it is a means of getting in.

clue.text: One such as Adam, cunning in metalwork

parts.note: Adam Smith was the Scottish economist, so he is one Smith
craft can mean guile or cunning

explanation.surface: Someone like Adam proves crafty at working metal.
explanation.definitionFit: The skill of a blacksmith or other worker in iron is the craft of forging metal.

clue.text: Blue a quid? Only half that on article

indicators.note: in a down clue the earlier pieces sit on top of the article
only the first half of the word quid is wanted, two of its four letters

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A puzzled query whether something blue costs a pound, then only half that price.
explanation.definitionFit: Aqua is a light greenish-blue colour, so it names a shade of blue.

clue.text: Insect in tree climbing for cover

indicators.note: the insect is placed inside the other piece
in a down clue climbing means the word reads upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: the elm is a tree
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: An insect scales a tree to find shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns ELM to MLE, which then holds ANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantle is a cloak or a covering layer, as a mantle of snow covers the ground.

clue.text: Officers sound nuts

indicators.note: sound here means said aloud, so the word for the officers is matched by how it is spoken

parts.note: colonels are senior army officers

explanation.surface: An insult claiming that officers sound crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' reads as an adjective meaning mad; here it is the plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The edible part inside a nutshell is its kernel, so kernels can be called nuts.

clue.text: Record — one in honour of the setter, an exemplar

parts.note: EP is an extended-play record
I is the Roman numeral one
to, as in a toast drunk to someone, means in their honour
the setter refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: A recording made as a tribute to the compiler, held up as a model.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is the perfect example of its type serves as its model or exemplar.

clue.text: Settle's marketplace perhaps under repair

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, linking the definition settle to the wordplay

parts.note: a market square is one kind of town square
a road that is up is being dug up for repair

explanation.surface: The Yorkshire town of Settle has its market square under repair.
explanation.walkthrough: Settle is a market town in North Yorkshire, which makes the capital look like a proper name.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle a bill or a quarrel is to pay up or sort it out with the other party.

clue.text: Intricately shape stripped pine and start to use with caution

indicators.note: worked intricately suggests the letters of shape are rearranged
stripped means the outer letters of pine are peeled away

explanation.surface: A woodworker carefully shapes some bare pine before using it.
explanation.definitionFit: Introducing a scheme gradually, step by step, is bringing it in cautiously.

clue.text: Flier and French disciplinarian

parts.note: a martin is a bird of the swallow family
et is French for and

explanation.surface: A pilot who is French and a strict enforcer of rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flier' suggests a pilot; it is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A martinet is a strict stickler for rules, named after a severe French drillmaster.

clue.text: Alphabet design recomposed after penny drops

indicators.note: the letters are redesigned into a new arrangement
drops means the letter for penny falls out of the word

explanation.surface: A typeface for the alphabet is reworked once someone finally understands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after penny drops' looks like the idiom for understanding; it says remove P from RECOMPOSED, leaving RECOMOSED for 'design' to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The signalling system of dots and dashes assigns a pattern to each letter, an alphabet of its own.

clue.text: Profound notes of sex appeal enfolding foremost among actresses

indicators.note: enfolding means the first piece wraps around the next

parts.note: oomph is slang for sex appeal

indicators.note: foremost among picks the leading letter of actresses

explanation.surface: Deep notes with the allure that the leading actresses wrap themselves in.
explanation.definitionFit: The sound of a tuba or brass band is a deep rhythmic bass, so low notes.

clue.text: 'Brain' partly solved clue about revolutionary motorway

indicators.note: the shuffled clue letters go about the next piece
a clue that is solved has been worked out, so its letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: a revolutionary is a rebel
M is for motorway, as in the M1

explanation.surface: A brainy solver cracks part of a clue about an insurgent on the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solved' shuffles the letters to CELU; 'about' then wraps them round the rebel, before M is added.
explanation.definitionFit: The cerebellum is the region at the back of the brain that coordinates movement, so a portion of it.

clue.text: Newly-wed, having trip into Bulgaria, fell over

indicators.note: into says the trip goes inside the country code

parts.note: BG is the international code for Bulgaria
a ride is a trip or journey

indicators.note: over means the hill word is turned back to front

parts.note: a fell is upland moor in northern England

explanation.surface: A newlywed tumbled while on a trip through Bulgaria.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fell' reads as a verb, but it is the noun for a moor; 'over' reverses MOOR to ROOM.
explanation.definitionFit: A man just married on his wedding day is the husband of the new bride.

clue.text: Row with joiner

definitions.meaning: a row of seats, one level above another
one who ties things together, playfully read as tie-er

explanation.surface: An argument with a carpenter.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is one line of seats in a stack; read whimsically, someone who ties knots joins things.

clue.text: Outsiders on tour with old McKellen, for one — serious actor

indicators.note: the outer letters of the word tour are taken

parts.note: aged means old
Ian McKellen, the actor, is one Ian

explanation.surface: Outsiders on a tour with the veteran Sir Ian McKellen, a heavyweight of the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor known for tragic roles plays serious drama rather than comedy.

clue.text: NT at twelve?

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for noon and T for time, so the two words of the phrase shrink to these two letters

explanation.surface: A query about a theatre's show at twelve o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: NT suggests the National Theatre; it is what the answer's two words abbreviate to.
explanation.definitionFit: Midday, twelve o'clock, is the hour of the day the phrase names.

clue.text: Gold tint finally overlaying abstract painting — this might be a spoiler!

indicators.note: in a down clue the earlier pieces lie on top of the art movement

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: finally takes the closing letter of the word tint

parts.note: op art is abstract painting using optical effects

explanation.surface: A gold tint laid over an abstract canvas would ruin it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoiler' suggests something that ruins, but it is the aerodynamic fin fitted to a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A rear spoiler is a component bolted onto a car, so a vehicle component.

clue.text: A good many high-class Military Police holding youth down

indicators.note: the earlier pieces hold up the youth, which sits below them in the down entry

parts.note: U is short for upper-class, as in U and non-U
a teen is a young person

explanation.surface: Plenty of upper-crust military police are pinning a youngster to the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' looks like a container, but with 'down' it means the youth comes below the other pieces in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal word for an indefinitely large number means lots, a great many.

clue.text: Mean to correct a bloomer

indicators.note: to correct something is to set it right, so these letters are put into a new order

parts.note: a means one

explanation.surface: Intending to put right a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' suggests a mistake, but it is a flower; 'to correct' turns MEAN into ANEM.
explanation.definitionFit: This plant of the buttercup family bears showy flowers, so it is something that blooms.

clue.text: 'Soapsuds' oddly lacking as piece of work

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters of the word are missing, leaving the second, fourth, sixth and eighth

explanation.surface: A job done without enough washing-up suds.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical or literary composition is a work, catalogued by number.

clue.text: Remote inn's concocted soup

indicators.note: something concocted is cooked up, so the letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: An isolated tavern has cooked up a broth.
explanation.definitionFit: This thick Italian vegetable broth with pasta is a classic soup.

clue.text: Tip one's hat to Sarah, aboard Digger's truck

indicators.note: in a down clue the name sits on top of the vehicle, as if riding in it

parts.note: Sal is a short form of Sarah
a Digger is an Australian, and a ute is an Australian utility pick-up truck

explanation.surface: Raising one's hat to Sarah as she rides on the back of an Australian's pick-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digger' suggests an excavator; it is slang for an Australian.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising one's hat is a gesture of greeting or respect, the same as giving a salute.

clue.text: Pointer possibly showing 'open' tucked into goods

indicators.note: the word for open is put inside the other piece

parts.note: G is short for good, so two goods are G and G
to undo a parcel is to open it

explanation.surface: A finger shows where to open a parcel of goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pointer' suggests an arrow or a finger; it is a breed of hunting dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The pointer is a breed trained to stand and point at game for hunters.

clue.text: Model typist working overtime?

parts.note: a temp is a temporary office worker, often a typist
working late means staying past normal hours

explanation.surface: A fashion model has a temporary typing job and works extra hours.
explanation.definitionFit: A pattern or guide shape used to make copies serves as a model.

clue.text: 'Spitting Image' somewhat left-wing?

indicators.note: somewhat means only part of the words is used, letters inside left-wing

explanation.surface: Was the satirical puppet show Spitting Image a bit leftist?
explanation.walkthrough: Spitting Image was a British TV satire with puppets; here the phrase means an exact likeness.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's spitting image is their exact double, as alike as identical siblings.

clue.text: Token of oilman's excitement about launch in Notts

indicators.note: the launch of a word is its first letter
excitement stirs the letters up and about into a new order

parts.note: the oilman's letters are the fodder; the 's ties them to the excitement

explanation.surface: A small sign of an oil worker's thrill at a launch in Nottinghamshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Notts is short for Nottinghamshire, an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: A token payment is one in name only, a small sum, so the adjective means slight or symbolic.

clue.text: German's a mug? Far from it!

parts.note: ein is the German word for a
a stein is a large beer mug, from German

explanation.surface: Is a German a fool? Not at all!
explanation.walkthrough: 'mug' reads as a fool, so 'Far from it!' points to the famous German-born genius.
explanation.definitionFit: Far from being a fool, the physicist behind relativity is the byword for genius.

clue.text: 'May sadly embraces retreat.' Pardon?

indicators.note: embraces means the jumbled letters wrap around the retreat
sadly means the letters of May are disturbed into a new order

parts.note: a nest is a snug retreat or hideaway

explanation.surface: A newspaper headline saying Theresa May reluctantly accepts a withdrawal, then asks to be heard again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' turns MAY into AMY, which then holds NEST.
explanation.definitionFit: An official pardon granted to many offenders at once is a general amnesty.
